## Example 2.6(a) · Ferris-wheel heights {#fgt2-ferris-constants .trig-lesson .application-lesson .application-dense}

Anna is sitting in a carriage of a Ferris wheel which is revolving. The height, $A(t)$ in metres above the ground of the top of her carriage is given by:

$$A(t)=c-k\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{24}\right),$$

where $t$ is the time in seconds after Anna's carriage first reaches the bottom of its revolution and $c$ and $k$ are constants.

The top of each carriage reaches a greatest height of 39 m and a smallest height of 3 m.

**a)** Find the values of $c$ and $k$. **(2 marks)**

```{=html}
<div data-periodic="ferris-constants" class="periodic-demo"></div>
```

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 34 · Example 2.6 · HSC Advanced 2024 Q28 (Adapted)</p>

::: notes

Preserve the booklet's c and k: here c is the blue midline value and k is the orange amplitude magnitude. This differs from the role of k in our general form y=a cos nt+k; do not silently rename the source question. Greatest height c+k=39; smallest c−k=3. Add: 2c=42, so c=21. Subtract: 2k=36, so k=18. At t=0, A(0)=21−18=3, so the negative cosine starts at the minimum. The comparison with the general form is a=−18, n=π/24, midline=21. Reveal constants after working in OneNote. Allow about 5 minutes.

:::
